operations.specification: Create a new guest record in todo_app_guests with a generated UUID id and current timestamps for created_at and updated_at. Then create a corresponding guest session record in todo_app_guest_sessions with: generated UUID id, the guest's id as todo_app_guest_id, ip/href/referrer extracted from the request body, created_at set to now, expired_at set to now + session duration (e.g., 24 hours). Generate a JWT access token containing the guest id as a claim, and use the session id as the refresh token. Return both tokens in the response.
operations.description:
Create a new anonymous guest identity and session.

Guests are unauthenticated visitors who have not yet signed up or logged into the application. This operation creates a lightweight guest record in the `todo_app_guests` table along with an associated session in `todo_app_guest_sessions`. The session tracks the guest's IP address, entry page URL (`href`), and referring page URL (`referrer`) for basic analytics and security auditing.

Upon successful creation, the guest receives an authorized response containing an access token (JWT) and a refresh token. The refresh token corresponds to the session identifier and can be used to obtain new access tokens when the current one expires. Guests must provide this refresh token to extend their anonymous session.

This is the only entry point for unauthenticated visitors to obtain guest-level access. Once a guest transitions to a member via sign-up or login, the guest record is discarded.

requestBody.description: Guest registration payload containing session context information (IP address, entry URL, referrer) needed to establish the anonymous session.

responseBody.description: Authorization tokens granting the guest access to refresh their session. Contains an access token (JWT) for authenticated API calls and a refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Validate the incoming refresh token from the request body. Look up the corresponding session in todo_app_guest_sessions where id matches the refresh token value. Verify the session has not expired (expired_at > now). If valid, check that the session's guest (todo_app_guest_id) still exists in todo_app_guests. Generate a new JWT access token containing the guest id claim. Optionally extend the session's expired_at. Return new tokens. If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or the guest no longer exists, return 401 Unauthorized.
operations.description:
Refresh an existing guest session and obtain new authorization tokens.

Guests can extend their anonymous session by providing a valid refresh token obtained from a previous `join` or `refresh` operation. The system validates the token by looking up the corresponding session record in the `todo_app_guest_sessions` table and verifying that the session has not expired and that the associated guest record still exists in `todo_app_guests`.

On success, a new access token is issued for continued anonymous access. This operation does not create a new guest record or session — it only refreshes the existing session's authorization. The refresh token corresponds to the session ID created during the initial `join` operation or the most recent `refresh`.

If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or the guest record has been deleted (e.g., because the guest signed up as a member), the request is rejected with an authentication error. The guest must then create a new session via the `join` operation.

requestBody.description: Refresh token payload containing the session's refresh token to validate and exchange for new authorization tokens.

responseBody.description: New authorization tokens for the refreshed guest session. Contains an access token (JWT) for authenticated API calls and a refresh token for subsequent refresh operations.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Register a new member account. Validate that email is unique (check todo_app_members.email unique constraint). Hash the provided password using bcrypt. Create a new todo_app_members record. Create a todo_app_profiles record with the optional display_name. Create a todo_app_member_sessions record with IP/href/referrer from request context. Generate JWT access+refresh tokens. Return the tokens in IAuthorized response. On duplicate email, return 409 Conflict.
operations.description:
Create a new member account and establish an authenticated session.

This endpoint registers a new member using an email address and password. The email serves as the member's unique login identifier and cannot be changed later. The password is securely hashed before storage. An optional display name can be provided for the member's profile.

Upon successful registration, the member is immediately authenticated: a session is created, and JWT access and refresh tokens are returned. The member can then access all features within their private workspace.

If the email address is already registered, the endpoint returns a conflict error. Email addresses are case-sensitive and must be unique across all members.

requestBody.description: Registration credentials including email, password, and optional display name.

responseBody.description: JWT access and refresh tokens for the newly authenticated member session.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate an existing member. Look up the member by email in todo_app_members. Verify the provided password against password_hash using bcrypt.compare(). On success, create a new todo_app_member_sessions record with IP/href/referrer. Generate new JWT access+refresh tokens. On invalid credentials, return 401 Unauthorized.
operations.description:
Authenticate an existing member and establish an authenticated session.

This endpoint verifies the member's identity by confirming that the provided password matches the registered email address. The email must already exist in the system (the member must have registered first).

Upon successful authentication, a new session is created in the member_sessions table, and JWT access and refresh tokens are returned. The session captures the client IP address and page URL for audit purposes. The member can then access all features within their private workspace until the session expires or they log out.

If the email is not found or the password does not match, the endpoint returns an unauthorized error.

requestBody.description: Authentication credentials with email and password.

responseBody.description: JWT access and refresh tokens for the authenticated member session.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Validate the refresh token from the request body. Verify JWT signature and expiration. Look up the associated member in todo_app_members (check member exists). Create a new todo_app_member_sessions record. Issue new JWT access+refresh tokens. On invalid or expired refresh token, return 401 Unauthorized.
operations.description:
Renew JWT access and refresh tokens using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint allows a member to obtain new tokens without re-entering their credentials. The refresh token from the previous authentication is validated for signature and expiration. If valid, a new session is created, and fresh access and refresh tokens are issued.

This is useful for maintaining long-lived sessions. The old refresh token is not invalidated (standard JWT stateless pattern). Tokens expire naturally based on their expiration claims.

If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or malformed, the endpoint returns an unauthorized error.

requestBody.description: The refresh token to validate and exchange for new tokens.

responseBody.description: New JWT access and refresh tokens for continued authenticated access.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Creates a new anonymous guest session for an unauthenticated visitor.

When an unauthenticated user first accesses the application, the system initializes a guest record and creates an anonymous session for tracking purposes. The guest provides their current page URL (href) and the referring page URL (referrer) as context for the session.

The session is time-limited and expires after a predefined duration. Once expired, the guest must obtain a new session. Guest sessions are ephemeral and carry no persistent user data — all session state is discarded upon expiration or when the guest transitions to a member through sign-up or login.

This is the only operation available to guests before authentication, alongside the sign-up and login endpoints.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new guest record in todo_app_guests table with generated UUID and current timestamp.

Then create a new guest session in todo_app_guest_sessions table:
- Generate a new UUID for the session ID
- Set todo_app_guest_id to the newly created guest's ID
- Capture client IP from request headers (X-Forwarded-For or connection remote address)
- Set href and referrer from the request body
- Set created_at to current timestamp
- Set expired_at to current timestamp + session duration (e.g., 30 minutes)

Return the created guest record with its session token and expiration time.

Edge cases:
- If href or referrer are empty strings, store them as provided
- IP should be extracted from trusted proxy headers if behind a reverse proxy

responseBody.description: The created guest record including its session token and expiration timestamp for anonymous browsing.

requestBody.description: Session initialization data including the current page URL the guest is accessing and the HTTP referrer.

operations.description:
Retrieve a guest record by its unique identifier.

Guests are anonymous, unauthenticated visitors who have not yet signed up or logged into the application. Each guest record serves as a lightweight identifier tracking the visitor's anonymous presence. The record contains only basic metadata (creation and update timestamps); session-level details such as IP address, page URLs, and expiration are stored separately in related session records.

This operation returns the guest record for the specified identifier. If no guest exists with the given ID, a 404 Not Found response is returned.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query todo_app_guests table by primary key id. Return the full guest record if found. If no record matches the given guestId, return 404 Not Found. No joins needed as this returns only the guest record itself. Guest records are never soft-deleted — they are hard-deleted when the guest transitions to a member or when sessions expire.

responseBody.description: The guest record containing the guest's unique identifier and timestamps.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the guest record to retrieve. (global scope)
parameters.name: guestId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of the authenticated member's login sessions.

Sessions are automatically created each time the member logs in and track the origin (IP address, page URL, referrer) along with creation and expiration timestamps. This endpoint allows members to review their active and past sessions for security monitoring — for example, identifying unrecognized locations or devices.

Each session entry includes the IP address, the page where the session was initiated, the referrer, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp. Members can determine which sessions are still active (not yet expired) and which have already expired.

Results are paginated and sortable by creation date. Filtering by session status (active or expired) and creation date range is supported.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_member_sessions table filtered by the authenticated member's ID (todo_app_member_id).

Support the following search criteria in the request body:
- Filter by session status: 'active' (expired_at > current time) or 'expired' (expired_at <= current time), or 'all' (no filter)
- Filter by created_at date range (from/to)
- Pagination with page number and limit
- Sort by created_at ascending or descending (most recent first is default)

Return IPageITodoAppMemberSession.ISummary with:
- id: session UUID
- ip: client IP address
- href: page URL where session was initiated
- referrer: HTTP referrer
- created_at: session creation timestamp
- expired_at: session expiration timestamp
- isActive: computed boolean (expired_at > now)

No soft-delete filtering needed — sessions are hard-deleted on cascade when the member is deleted, and there is no deleted_at column on this table.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of session summary records containing identifying information (IP, URL, referrer) and timestamps for each login session.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for listing member sessions, including status filter (active/expired/all), creation date range, sort direction, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieves detailed information about a specific authenticated session belonging to the member.

This endpoint returns the security metadata associated with a member's session, including the IP address from which the session was initiated, the entry page URL (href), the HTTP referrer, and the session's creation and expiration timestamps. Each session is uniquely tied to the authenticated member — the system enforces that members can only view their own sessions.

Session metadata is useful for security auditing and monitoring, allowing members to verify from where and when their sessions were created. Expired sessions remain accessible for reference but cannot be used for authentication.

If the specified session does not exist or does not belong to the authenticated member, a not-found error is returned without disclosing whether the session ID is invalid or belongs to another member.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_member_sessions table by the provided sessionId (UUID primary key).

Ensure data isolation: the authenticated member's ID must match todo_app_member_id in the retrieved record. If no record is found for the given sessionId, or if the record exists but belongs to a different member, return a 404 Not Found error without distinguishing between "session not found" and "session belongs to another member."

No relationships need to be joined — return all columns of the session record as-is. The session is append-only and never modified after creation, so no locking or transaction isolation is needed.

Edge cases:
- Expired sessions: return the session data as normal (expired_at field indicates expiration). Do not filter out expired sessions.
- Deleted member accounts: sessions are cascade-deleted when the member is deleted, so this query will return no results.

responseBody.description: The member session object containing session metadata including IP address, entry URL, referrer, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the session to retrieve. Must correspond to a session owned by the authenticated member.
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member's own profile information.

This operation allows an authenticated member to update their personal profile settings — specifically their display name. The member is identified through their authentication session (JWT token), so no path parameter is required. The display name is optional and visible only to the member themselves in this private todo application.

The update modifies the member's one-to-one profile record in the todo_app_profiles table. Other member attributes such as email and password are not managed through this endpoint — email is immutable after account creation, and password changes have their own dedicated flow.

Only the authenticated member can update their own profile. Accessing or modifying another member's profile is prohibited and will result in an access-denied error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implementation guide:

1. Extract the authenticated member's ID from the JWT token in the Authorization header.

2. Validate the request body: display_name can be null (to clear the name) or a non-empty string. No other member fields should be mutable through this endpoint.

3. Query todo_app_profiles for the record matching the authenticated member's ID (todo_app_member_id). A profile always exists because it is created at registration.

4. Update the display_name field and set updated_at to the current timestamp.

5. Return the updated member data: query todo_app_members joined with todo_app_profiles to return id, email, display_name, created_at, updated_at.

6. Edge cases:
   - Unauthenticated request: reject with 401 Unauthorized.
   - display_name exceeding reasonable length (e.g., >255 chars): reject with 422 and validation error.
   - Member tries to update email or password_hash through this endpoint: silently ignore or reject those fields — they should not be part of the IUpdate DTO.

7. Use a database transaction to ensure the profile update and any related operations (audit logging) are atomic.

responseBody.description: The updated member profile containing the member's authentication identity (id, email) and profile information (display name) after applying the requested changes.

requestBody.description: Profile fields to update for the authenticated member. Only the display name can be modified through this endpoint. Fields not included in the request will retain their current values.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated member's own account information including profile details.

Returns the member's registered email address, current display name, and account creation and update timestamps. This is the primary endpoint for viewing one's own account details within the private workspace.

Strict data isolation is enforced — the authenticated member can only retrieve their own information. The {memberId} path parameter must match the authenticated member's identity. Any mismatch results in an authorization error (403 Forbidden), preventing access to other users' data.

Sensitive authentication credentials such as the password hash are excluded from the response. The display name is returned directly as part of the member object since each member has exactly one profile in a one-to-one relationship.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query todo_app_members table by primary key (id) matching the {memberId} path parameter. Include a LEFT JOIN with todo_app_profiles on todo_app_member_id to retrieve the display_name. Verify that the authenticated member's ID (extracted from the JWT token) matches the requested {memberId} — if they don't match, return a 403 Forbidden error. The SQL should select id, email, created_at, updated_at from members and display_name from profiles. Exclude password_hash and other internal fields. Return 404 Not Found if the member ID does not exist in the database. Use a single query with the join for efficiency.

responseBody.description: The authenticated member's account information including email, display name, and account timestamps. Excludes sensitive data such as the password hash.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target member (UUID primary key). Must match the authenticated member's own ID — accessing another member's data is strictly forbidden by the privacy policy.
parameters.name: memberId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of password reset requests for the authenticated member.

Each password reset record represents a request to reset the member's password. The list shows the reset code, creation timestamp, expiration timestamp, and consumption status (soft-delete timestamp). Results are paginated and can be filtered by date range or consumption status.

This operation requires authentication. Only the authenticated member's own password reset records are returned — no other member's data is accessible.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query todo_app_member_password_resets table filtered by the authenticated member's ID (todo_app_member_id). Apply pagination with page and limit parameters from the request body. Support optional filtering by date range on created_at. Support optional filtering by consumption status (deleted_at IS NULL vs deleted_at IS NOT NULL). Sort by created_at descending by default. Return paginated summary records. The code field should be masked or partially shown in the summary view for security.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of password reset record summaries for the authenticated member. Each summary includes the reset code, creation timestamp, expiration timestamp, and consumption status.

requestBody.description: Pagination parameters and optional filters for searching password reset records. Includes page number, page size, and optional date range or consumption status filters.

operations.description:
Retrieve a password reset record by its unique identifier to verify its validity for password recovery.

The response includes the reset record's status information, allowing the caller to determine whether the reset token is still valid (not expired and not yet consumed). This endpoint is used during the password reset flow after the user provides their reset code, enabling the frontend to verify the token's validity before proceeding with setting a new password.

Accessible only to guests and members who possess the reset identifier. The endpoint does not expose the sensitive reset code value in its response to maintain security.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the todo_app_member_password_resets table by primary key (id). Return the password reset record including its expiration status (expired_at compared against current time) and consumption status (deleted_at being null or non-null). If the record is not found, return a 404 Not Found error. The reset code itself should be excluded from the response for security — the caller already possesses the code.

responseBody.description: The password reset record with validity status information, including expiration timestamp and consumption status.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the password reset record to retrieve.
parameters.name: resetId

operations.description:
Retrieves the authenticated member's own profile information.

This endpoint returns the display name and metadata for the currently authenticated member's profile. Each member has exactly one profile created at registration. The profile is private — only the authenticated member can view their own profile. There is no mechanism to view another user's profile.

The display name is optional and can be updated through the profile update endpoint. If not set, display_name returns null.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query todo_app_profiles where todo_app_member_id matches the authenticated member's ID (resolved from JWT token). Return the profile record if found. Since a profile is created atomically with member registration (via cascade), a missing profile indicates a data integrity issue — return 404 Not Found. No joins needed. Return only fields: id, todo_app_member_id, display_name, created_at, updated_at.

responseBody.description: The authenticated member's profile containing display name, creation timestamp, and last update timestamp.

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member's profile information.

Only the display name can be modified through this endpoint. The display name is optional — it can be set, changed, or cleared. The update takes effect immediately and is reflected in subsequent profile retrievals.

This is a private profile accessible only to the owning member. No other user can view or modify this profile.

Authentication is required. The profile is identified by the authenticated member's identity from the JWT token, not from a path parameter.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Fetch the profile record belonging to the authenticated member using their member ID (extracted from JWT token). The profile is linked to the member via the todo_app_member_id foreign key.

Update the display_name field if provided in the request body. If display_name is null, clear the existing value. If display_name is absent from the request body, treat it as clearing the value.

Update the updated_at timestamp to the current time.

Return the updated profile record including all fields (id, todo_app_member_id, display_name, created_at, updated_at).

Edge cases:
- If the member has no profile yet (should not occur since profiles are created at registration), return a 404 Not Found error.
- The profile is identified by the authenticated member, so no authorization check beyond authentication is needed — the member can only access their own profile.

responseBody.description: The updated profile containing the member's display name and metadata timestamps.

requestBody.description: Profile update payload containing the new display name value. Set to null or omit to clear the display name.

operations.description:
Create a new todo in the authenticated member's private workspace.

The member provides a title (required) and may optionally include a description, start date, and due date. The todo is created in the incomplete state by default. The member's identity is automatically associated with the todo — no other member can access or view this todo.

The operation validates that the title is a non-empty, non-whitespace string. If both a start date and due date are provided, the due date must not precede the start date. Dates are date-only values (time components are semantically ignored).

Upon successful creation, the system returns the full todo object including its generated ID, creation timestamp, and initial state.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new record into todo_app_todos table.

1. Extract the authenticated member's ID from the request context (todo_app_member_id).
2. Validate the title:
   - Must be a non-empty string (not null, not empty, not whitespace-only).
3. Validate date constraints:
   - If both start_date and due_date are provided, verify due_date >= start_date.
   - Reject (400 Bad Request) if due_date precedes start_date.
   - Dates are date-only (time component is semantically ignored — store as-is but treat as date for comparison).
4. Set defaults:
   - completed_at: null (todo starts incomplete)
   - deleted_at: null (todo starts active)
   - created_at/updated_at: current timestamp
   - id: generate UUID
5. Insert the record.
6. The member_id is derived from the authenticated session, not from the request body. This enforces strict data isolation — members can only create todos in their own workspace.
7. Return the created todo record with all fields populated.

Error handling:
- 400: Missing or empty title, due_date before start_date
- 401: Unauthenticated request

responseBody.description: The newly created todo with all fields populated, including the generated ID and timestamps.

requestBody.description: Fields for creating a new todo. The title is required and must be non-empty. Description, start date, and due date are optional.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of the authenticated member's todo items with filtering by completion status and customizable sorting.

The returned list displays each todo's title, completion status (derived from completed_at), start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date. Deleted todos (soft-deleted with non-null deleted_at) are excluded from this list and can only be accessed via the trash endpoint.

Filtering supports three completion status modes: all todos, only complete todos (non-null completed_at), and only incomplete todos (null completed_at). Sorting supports ascending or descending order by creation date, start date, or due date. When sorting by start date or due date ascending, todos with null values appear at the end of the results.

This operation enforces strict data isolation — only todos belonging to the authenticated member are returned.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query todo_app_todos where todo_app_member_id = authenticated member ID AND deleted_at IS NULL. Apply completion status filter based on the request's status field: 'all' (no filter), 'complete' (completed_at IS NOT NULL), 'incomplete' (completed_at IS NULL). Apply sorting based on the request's sortBy and sortOrder fields: supported sortBy values are 'created_at', 'start_date', 'due_date'; sortOrder is 'asc' or 'desc'. For start_date and due_date ascending, use NULLS LAST ordering. Implement cursor-based pagination or offset-based pagination using page/pageSize from the request body. Return IPageITodoAppTodo.ISummary with pagination metadata and the todo summary records mapped from the query results. The summary should include: id, title, completed_at, start_date, due_date, created_at.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo summary records containing title, completion status, start date, due date, and creation date.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering, sorting, and paginating the member's todo list. Includes completion status filter, sort field and direction, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single todo item with all its details.

Returns the full todo entity including title, description, start date, due date, completion status, timestamps, and other metadata. The authenticated member can only retrieve todos they own — attempting to access another member's todo returns a not-found error without distinguishing between non-existent and inaccessible records.

This operation does not include edit history; use the dedicated edit history endpoint for that information.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_todos table by the given todoId (UUID primary key).

1. Fetch the todo record where id = todoId AND todo_app_member_id = authenticated member's id.
2. If no record is found (either because the todo doesn't exist or it belongs to another user), return a 404 Not Found error. Do NOT distinguish between 'not found' and 'not owned' to prevent data leakage.
3. Return the full entity with all fields: id, todo_app_member_id, title, description, start_date, due_date, completed_at, deleted_at, created_at, updated_at.
4. The todo can be active (deleted_at IS NULL) or in trash (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) — both are accessible via this endpoint for the owner.
5. No request body is needed as this is a GET operation.

responseBody.description: Full todo entity containing all fields including title, description, start/end dates, completion status, timestamps, and ownership information.

parameters.description: UUID primary key of the todo item to retrieve. Must be a valid UUID owned by the authenticated member.
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Updates an existing todo's editable fields (title, description, start date, due date) for the authenticated member.

This operation allows the member who owns the todo to modify its title, description, start date, and/or due date. Only the fields explicitly provided in the request body are updated; omitted fields retain their current values. The todo must be active (not in trash) to be edited.

Each edit automatically generates an immutable history entry in the todo's edit history, recording which fields were changed and their new values. History entries are timestamped and sorted from most recent to oldest.

A todo that has been soft-deleted (in trash) cannot be edited. To edit a trashed todo, restore it first.

Only the owning member can update their todos. Attempting to update another user's todo results in a not-found error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Validate the todo exists and belongs to the authenticated member (todo_app_member_id matches the authenticated user's ID). If the todo is soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL), reject with an error — trashed todos cannot be edited. Update only the provided fields in the request body: title, description, start_date, due_date. Set updated_at to the current timestamp. After updating, create an edit history entry in todo_app_edit_histories recording which fields changed — include only the new values for changed fields (title, description, start_date, due_date), with unchanged fields set to null. The history entry's created_at is set to the current timestamp. Return the updated ITodoAppTodo on success. If the todo does not exist or belongs to another user, return a not-found error without distinguishing between the two cases.

responseBody.description: The complete updated todo entity with all fields reflecting the applied changes.

parameters.description: The UUID identifier of the todo to update.
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Editable fields for the todo: title (required), description (optional), start date (optional), and due date (optional). Only provided fields will be updated; omitted optional fields remain unchanged.

prerequisites.description: The todo item must exist before it can be updated. POST /todoApp/member/todos creates the todo that is later referenced by todoId in the update operation.

operations.description:
Toggle the completion status of a todo item belonging to the authenticated member.

Calling this endpoint marks an incomplete todo as complete, or marks a complete todo as incomplete. This is a simple binary toggle — the endpoint only accepts PUT with no request body, and toggles the internal `completed_at` timestamp to reflect the new state.

Only the owner of the todo can perform this operation. Members cannot toggle completion status on another user's todos. Trashed (soft-deleted) todos cannot be toggled — an error is returned if the todo is in the trash.

The response returns the full updated todo entity with the new completion state reflected in the completed_at field (null = incomplete, timestamp = complete).
operations.name: complete
operations.specification:
1. Retrieve the todo by {todoId} from todo_app_todos table.
2. Verify the authenticated member's id matches todo_app_member_id. If not, reject with access-denied error.
3. Verify deleted_at IS NULL (todo is not trashed). If trashed, reject with error — completion toggle is not allowed on trashed todos.
4. Toggle the completed_at field:
   - If completed_at IS NULL → set to current UTC timestamp (mark as complete)
   - If completed_at IS NOT NULL → set to NULL (mark as incomplete)
5. Update the updated_at timestamp to current UTC time.
6. Return the updated ITodoAppTodo entity with all fields.

responseBody.description: The updated todo entity reflecting the new completion status after the toggle operation.

parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the todo whose completion status will be toggled.
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: The todo must be created before its completion status can be toggled. POST /todoApp/member/todos creates a new todo in the member's workspace, producing the todo entity identified by todoId that this operation modifies.

operations.description:
Soft-delete a todo item and move it to the trash.

The system performs a soft delete on the specified todo, setting a `deleted_at` timestamp and moving it to the user's trash. Once deleted, the todo no longer appears in the user's normal todo list, filtered views, or sorted views of active todos. All of the todo's data — including its title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and edit history — is preserved in the system for potential recovery.

To permanently remove the todo from the trash, use the permanent delete endpoint. To restore a deleted todo back to the active list, use the restore endpoint.

Only the todo owner can delete their own todo. Attempting to delete another member's todo returns a not-found error (without distinguishing between non-existent and inaccessible todos). Deleting an already-deleted (trashed) todo returns a rejection error.
